summary: KV prefetch ordering causing intermittent p99 latency bursts on repeat prompts
description:
Issue summary: Customers report sporadic, high p99 response times on repeat prompts (identical prefix + same completion request) from AtlasHealth's dedicated pool.
Impact: ~15% of requests in a 1-hour window hit p99 > 3s (baseline 250ms). No 5xxs, but many client-side timeouts. Affects production dedicated cluster in us-west; customer API retries amplify load.
Environment: prod dedicated cluster (pool-id d-az1-west-3), autoscaled GPU nodes, prefix/KV cache enabled with prefetching.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Use AtlasHealth example prompt A (included in attachment).
2) Send series of identical chat requests at 50 rps with short inter-call gaps for 5 minutes.
3) Observe intermittent latency spikes on repeat invocations; spikes correlated with prefetch log entries.
Expected behavior: Repeat prompts should hit KV/prefix cache and return near-cache-hit latency (~200-350ms p99).
Actual behavior: Intermittent cache-miss-like behavior; backend logs show out-of-order prefetch completion causing duplicate cold reads and contention.
Logs / evidence:
- Grafana trace: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/serve-traces?orgId=1&var-pool=d-az1-west-3
- Snapshot of NGINX timings and client timeouts attached (s3://redwood-support/att/SUP-94218/nginx_times.csv)
- Serving-runtime logs show prefetch:request_id order mismatches and repeated shard reads around timestamps 2026-03-13T15:22:10Z-15:28:00Z.
Investigation notes:
- SRE reproduced locally by replaying customer traffic; enabling verbose kv-prefetch logs shows prefetch tasks queued and completed non-deterministically when parallelism > 8.
- Hypothesis: Prefetch queue ordering not preserving request affinity, leading to hot-shard serialization and duplicate KV fetches; combined with autoscaler churn creates transient disk I/O spikes on shard leaders.
- Observed correlation between prefetch task reordering and high queueing latency in the serving runtime's prefetch worker pool (worker-starvation traces attached).
Temporary mitigation applied:
- Disabled aggressive prefetch for AtlasHealth pool (set prefetch.concurrency=4) at 2026-03-13T18:05Z — p99 reduced from ~3.2s to ~420ms in next 30m window.
- Added retry budget increase for client-side retries to avoid amplifying load; advised customer to reduce short-interval retries while mitigation in flight.
Next steps / action items:
- SRE/Runtime: implement request-affinity ordering in prefetch queue to prioritize in-flight request prefixes (PR drafted: related_github_prs above). Owner: Ethan Brooks. ETA: 5d.
- Runtime: add metrics to surface prefetch queueing depth and per-shard inflight prefetch counters. Owner: Priya Singh. ETA: 3d.
- Ops: investigate autoscaler churn during the spike window; correlate node rebalances with prefetch saturation. Owner: Diego Ruiz. ETA: 2d.
- CS: follow up with AtlasHealth with RCA and temporary config change details, confirm customer-side retry adjustments. Owner: Maya Patel. ETA: 1d.
- Postmortem and runbook update after fix is rolled out.
Resolution notes: partial mitigation applied by reducing prefetch concurrency; code change in review to enforce ordering. Will keep ticket open until PR merged and deployed to prod and customer confirms stable latencies.
